clue.text: Dance with energy and desire

parts.note: to hop is to dance or skip lightly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dancer moves with vigour and longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wish or longing for something is a hope.

clue.text: Sufferer from lumbago may restrain from action

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad back might keep themselves from doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a lumbago sufferer may clutch their aching back.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to refrain or keep oneself or another from acting is to hold back; literally, gripping one's sore lumbar region.

clue.text: Father's friend has caged a bird

indicators.note: the friend's letters enclose the other pieces as a cage holds a bird

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A dad's mate keeps a bird in a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: something that belongs to or comes from a father is paternal.

clue.text: Government department's feature that may suit self‑employed writer?

definitions.text: feature that may suit self‑employed writer

explanation.surface: A Whitehall ministry is described as handy for a freelance author.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Office is the UK ministry for policing and immigration; a freelance writer may also work from an office at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of a British ministry, and literally a study in one's house for working.

clue.text: Like an egg that's old and useless

parts.note: a void cheque or contract is invalid and of no use

explanation.surface: An egg that is past it and worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Shape word: something egg-shaped, oval in three dimensions, is described thus.

clue.text: First-class old mini-dwelling ending with the National Trust

parts.note: ex- means former, so old
a cell is a tiny room such as a monk's or prisoner's

indicators.note: the final letter of the word 'the' is taken

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A fine old cottage passes into the care of a heritage body.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that owns historic houses and landscapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something of the highest quality is outstanding, first-rate.

clue.text: Quartet outside small room full of zest?

indicators.note: the group of four is wrapped around the room

parts.note: a group of four is a foursome
lav, short for lavatory, is a small room

explanation.surface: Four people gather round a tiny space, bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zest' is citrus peel used for flavour, so 'full of zest' hints at tasty rather than energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun on zest as peel: food packed with taste is flavoursome.

clue.text: Trendy action for sure

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: A fashionable gesture, without doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an emphatic word meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: I get so nasty as self-centred person

indicators.note: the letters turn nasty, unruly, and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to becoming unpleasant through selfishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person absorbed in their own interests is an egotist or egoist.

clue.text: Reluctant to shed outer bits of clothes

indicators.note: the opening C and the closing ES of the word clothes are stripped away

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to take off their outer garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C from the front and ES from the back of CLOTHES leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unwilling, as in being loath or loth to go.

clue.text: Copper about to join worker in African country? That's risky

indicators.note: the copper and worker go inside the country's name

parts.note: Togo is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the copper symbol is turned around

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A police officer joins a labourer in Africa, which is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an uncertain, precarious situation is described as touch-and-go.

clue.text: Saint and sailors wearing fuzz

indicators.note: the beard is worn around the sailors

parts.note: facial fuzz is a beard
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors are dressed in something fluffy, a holy man perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: St Bernard is a saint, after whom the rescue dog is named.

clue.text: Expects fun and games will be interrupted by one head

indicators.note: the other pieces break into the word for pranks

parts.note: antics are playful pranks
I is the Roman numeral one
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A head teacher stops the fun, as foreseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look forward to or foresee something is to expect it.

clue.text: A female with some pride?

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, so a female member of one is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun pun: a she-cat of the big-cat family living in a pride.

clue.text: One to crow as heretic, clan getting disturbed

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A heretic boasts as his clan is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the traditional name for a rooster in fables such as Chaucer's.
explanation.definitionFit: Name for a cockerel, a bird that crows at dawn in folk tales.

clue.text: Able to take part, not having lost heart

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word not is dropped

explanation.surface: Fit to take part, still keen despite setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone capable or skilled is competent.

clue.text: New Lab. has one formal procedure deriving from its founder?

indicators.note: new signals the letters of Lab are made afresh in another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rite is a formal ceremony

explanation.surface: New Labour has a ritual inherited from the man who founded it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair launched New Labour, the British party rebrand of the 1990s; his followers are Blairites.
explanation.definitionFit: Political label: following the founder of New Labour, Tony Blair.

clue.text: Sweet female opening charity event with tirade

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity fundraiser
a rant is a long angry speech

explanation.surface: A lovely woman opens a fundraiser with an outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is when UK students raise money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense of smell: sweet-smelling, perfumed.

clue.text: Financial executive given wave by politician in bed

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is a Member of Parliament
a roller is a long ocean wave

explanation.surface: A finance chief is greeted by an MP lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Job title: a controller of accounts in a company or government.

clue.text: Disown bombast that goes around the City

parts.note: rant is bombastic talk
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Rejecting pompous talk that circulates in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take back or renounce a belief is to recant.

clue.text: Woman noted for work in market has closed early

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: the word has is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A trader shut up shop ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Martha, sister of Mary in the Gospels, busied herself with serving while Mary listened.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical figure: the sister in Luke's Gospel known for housework.

clue.text: Someone to emulate for instance

explanation.surface: A role model, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A model worth copying; and an illustrative case, as in 'for example'.

clue.text: Sympathy and money needed by Heather

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Kindness and cash are required by a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fellow feeling, emotional sensitivity to others.

clue.text: This monk is one who may deal with monkfish, we hear!

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds the same

parts.words: one who may deal with monkfish
parts.note: a fryer cooks fish

explanation.surface: A monk who cooks monkfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a friar is a member of a mendicant religious order.

clue.text: What critical PhD examiner may be, showing opposition

definitions.text: What critical PhD examiner may be

explanation.surface: A tough doctoral examiner shows hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits as ANTI THESIS: against the candidate's dissertation.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrast or direct opposite; literally against a doctoral dissertation.

clue.text: A lass hasn't left — is seen around port

the young woman no longer has the abbreviation for left, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: lass means girl

explanation.surface: A girl who stays is spotted near a harbour.

clue.text: Brief strain troubled politician

indicators.note: the letters are troubled and rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A short-lived tension worries a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lasting only a short time, fleeting.

clue.text: Remain idle

explanation.surface: Stay put and do nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay or be left in place; and to be inactive or relax.
